thread_title: Am I wasting my career here?
comment:
I started my career in WITCH companies in 2005. Now don't tell me I am old now :)

I loved to code and always wanted to develop an end to end software . 

In the IT service company, you always get a portion of something to develop, which might land in production, but you will never be able to see the impact of your work. This happens only if you are lucky enough to land up in a project where you are developing a software from scratch. Otherwise most people in IT services companies work in support projects.

After working for a WITCH, I switched to a small IT service company where I developed a product for Oracle. That company was closed, and I switched back to again a WITCH. I worked there for a couple of years and started working on my first startups. There I developed the entire product for the first time, deployed it on VPS but the startup closed after running it for 18 months. 

And I went back again to WITCH. But by this time it was clear to me that what I want, I will never get in the WITCH companies. So along with my job, I kept developing products for others(sometimes for free). And finally started again in 2015 and sold the company in 2019, though it was not a beach side exit.

Now why am I sharing my story here, not to tell how great the journey was, but my lack of awareness about what I really wanted during the initial years of my career , and where I can get what I really want.

I loved coding and developing software. If somebody had guided me to join a product based company like Zoho at that time, it would probably have been much easier and better. 

Coming back to your question, here are a few questions for you to answer :
A. Start by answering what is that you really get joy out of, when it comes to work.
B. Do you enjoy coding and developing software?
C. What skills you are lacking and  you can learn along with doing your job? 
D. If it's been more than 3 years in the same company, there is no harm in preparing for an interview. But think about what kind of company you want to join.

At the same time, chill and don't forget to enjoy your newly married life. 

Hope this helps

thread_title: Am I stupid for wanting to quit without an offer? 2 YOE, 10-15 hour shifts, toxic work culture, and severe burnout
comment:
I actually went through something really similar. I quit my last job without having another offer lined up because I genuinely couldn’t take it anymore.

It was a remote startup and I had joined around a year after graduating, so I was still pretty new to the industry. The culture there was  terrible. Everything was always urgent, everyone was stressed, and people loved blaming each other for every small thing. If something broke, even slightly, fingers immediately got pointed at the developer. There was barely any proper communication and people would literally shout at you on calls like basic respect didn’t exist.

There were only maybe two or three people there who were actually helpful. Everyone else just made work feel miserable.

The thing that finally pushed me over the edge was this one feature I was working on. We had a call with me, my PM, and my senior engineer. During the meeting, my senior explained one approach. But after the call, the PM told me to do it differently. We even discussed it for days and I built it exactly the way she explained.

Then about a week later, my senior engineer asked for an update and got really angry, saying this wasn’t what he had asked for. And the worst part was that later the PM called me separately and basically threw me under the bus. She started acting like she had explained everything properly and that I somehow misunderstood everything on my own. I still remember just sitting there thinking, “What the hell is happening right now?”

That day honestly broke me mentally. I realized no matter how much effort I put in, people would still protect themselves first and dump the blame on whoever they could.

So I resigned without any backup offer. Everyone says it’s risky and to this day,i think it is, but the second I put down my papers, I felt this massive relief. Like the constant anxiety just disappeared overnight. For the first time in months, I could breathe properly again.
So take your time, maybe a weekend off and just think through . Weight your options and just trust your gut as you only know what youre going through.

thread_title: People who stayed at TCS, what are the pros and cons of staying?
comment:
I can tell you why I stayed for 8 years. I'm sorry but this will be long as I feel very passionately about what I am about to say.

I got allocated to a manual testing project straight after ILP, in TCS Kolkata. The entire job was to run SQL queries in UAT env and checking if the difference with PROD is as expected. Sounds like a career killer right? That's what at least 20 people must have advised me back then. But my boss at the time said something else that changed my life.

For context, I was always a below average student. 67% in ISC and 7.1 DGPA in Btech (Tier 3). I swear, by the time I graduated (IT), I wouldn't have been able to even debug syntax errors in a C program that adds 2 numbers, let alone write one. Sadly that says more about the Education system in India than my academic prowess, but I digress.

Coming back to what my boss advised every early-career employee in the team. He said, "Think of the first 5 years of your career as a university where you get paid to learn. Don't prioritise growth over learning." He was a nice, polite man and I respected him a lot.

Armed with his wisdom, I focused on learning Credit Risk concepts (my project domain) and the equations and formulae used to calculate the risk metrics for investment banking products. TCS helped me with free LinkedIn learning and Udemy subscriptions. And the best part - TCS probably has the best library among all companies (they call them IRCs). The best textbooks, the best journals, research paper inventory, business magazines, you name it. Sadly they are mostly empty all the time. Suddenly, the meaningless DB outputs started making sense to me in the context of the client's business. I started enjoying my work and I understood the significance of it.

Fast forward 10 years (8 of them with TCS), still with just a Tier 3 BTech and zero certifications, I am blessed and immensely lucky to be a Director at one of the largest Investment Banks in the world (one of the youngest too in the same designation in my company). My monthly in-hand payout now is approx 32 times my first salary at TCS which I never imagined in my wildest dreams just 3 years back.

And I owe it all to TCS. It's not a company. It's an institution.

PS- It's also probably one of the most empathetic companies as well (or maybe I just had a great manager). They also arranged a bed in a hospital for my grandma during COVID Delta wave, when unicorns were probably easier to find than hospital beds.

thread_title: How to get rid of this TCS company. It's been only a week and I'm frustrated from TCS!!
comment:
Hmm, as someone who started from TCS, i feel like I should comment.

First things first, if you've already made up your mind, then sure, resign and pay the bond amount. (Can probably get away with not paying depending on the manager). 

So I joined TCS as fresher back in 2020, stayed there for 2 years. I don't know where my office is till now, i joined remote and left (corona times). So I can't really say much about your uniform issue. 

About ILP, i forgot which one it was, was it the one u do before joining? If so, that's fun man, easy 60k money from acing that test. I don't think i did any courses either, just went and gave exam. Got that sweet bonus. If it's something post joining, I'm honestly not sure. I don't remember going through anything specific. It's just normal corporate onboarding courses which every company has anyway. Get used to it. If it's T factor related thing, I'm pretty sure that's optional. I was in TCS digital, so it's possible I never went through whatever ILP is if it's not one of the things I listed above.

Now, why are you so sure it'll be support project? Too much external influence i guess. Yes, lots of support projects do get assigned to freshers, but that wasn't the case for me atleast. Within a week of joining TCS, i was put into a project and started working. I'm pretty sure by my 3rd week, I had a PR raised there. (I was in cloud BU, working on BFSI project). So honestly I don't have any complaints about the work I got back in TCS. Infact it layed the foundation for my career. Within 2 months, I got to take care of that entire project, so loads of responsibilities, it was fun. My manager shielded me from corporate politics as well. So I'll say give it a shot, maybe you'll get some good project like me. Otherwise, I'm pretty sure this is from RMG, so keep denying projects,.. what's the worst they can do? Remove you? That's what you want right? So all good. If they terminate, bond might not be enforced (unsure, but might be the case)


I used to be frustrated before I joined TCS (mostly because of the things I heard and read) , but my life at TCS was pretty fun NGL. Especially since I was remote. All I can say is try to change your perspective and things might look better. Let's assume you get support project, What's the issue? I just look at it as free time/money. You don't have too much stress, can slack off a lot. Meanwhile you can prepare for things you really wanna do, next switch, higher studies, exploring passion. Your life/career won't end just because you stayed in TCS...

 Don't stress about things not in your control. Take your time to upskill well, tcs will add those years of experience to your resume while you upskill. So neat.

The only part that's really bad from my perspective is that dreaded 90 days notice period. I won't even sugarcoat, that can be a major headache. Most companies will hang up as soon as they hear 90 days. What I used to do was lie about it being 2 months which can be further reduced to 1 by talking with my manager. In my case, i never planned to take the first offer, so this worked. Once i got first offer, i could use it for subsequent ones, and since I'll on notice period, and only 2/1 month would be left, I won't be lying anymore either. Besides, you could always say to the first company that some f up happened and you have to serve 3 months. But I've definitely resigned, here's the proof. Because see, once offer extended, even they don't wanna waste all their resources to look for alternate candidate. 

But yea, best of luck with your career man, don't fret too much. Take it as an adventure and have fun. Keep upskilling and all will be well. Save up money as emergency fund, would be of help if in worst case you get fed up and resign immediately and don't serve notice period (slightly unethical, but ppl do it).
